title: Open Sentences: Finding the Missing Number
seo_title: Open Sentences – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the missing number in open sentences with addition, subtraction, multiplication and division; write and solve number sentences from word problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on open sentences: missing numbers in addition, subtraction, multiplication and division, writing number sentences and solving problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: + and − undo each other; × and ÷ undo each other.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • An open sentence has a missing number, shown by a box □ or a letter.
  • Use the inverse operation: □ + 25 = 60 → □ = 60 − 25 = 35. □ × 6 = 54 → □ = 54 ÷ 6 = 9.
  • Check by putting your answer back in the sentence.

Examples

Example

□ − 48 = 75

75 + 48

Answer: 123

Example

I think of a number, × 4, + 5 = 33

33 − 5 = 28

28 ÷ 4

Answer: 7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the same operation□ + 25 = 60 needs subtraction, not addition.
Mixing up □ − 48 and 48 − □Read the order carefully.
Not checkingPut the number back in the box.

faq.a: An operation that undoes another: subtraction undoes addition.

faq.q: Can a letter be used instead of a box?
How do I write a number sentence from a story?

items.q: I think of a number, multiply it by 7 and add 10. The answer is 220. What is my number?
items.e: Work backwards: 220 − 10 = 210, then 210 ÷ 7 = 30.

items.q: Peter buys 3 books at the same price and gets ₦190 change from ₦430. How much does one book cost?
items.e: Cost of the books: ₦430 − ₦190 = ₦240. One book: ₦240 ÷ 3 = ₦80.
